title: Storage stack decision (SQLite / sqlite-vec / mxbai-embed-large)
notes: Clean, short, decision-dense session. No noise. Baseline case every extractor should do well on.

turns.text: We need to pick a database for astramemory-local. It has to run fully offline on a laptop, no server process. What do you recommend?

For a local-first, single-process daemon, SQLite is the right choice over Postgres — no server to manage, ships as a single file, and better-sqlite3 gives synchronous fast access from Node. Postgres would require the user to run a separate server, which conflicts with the 'local-first' goal.
Good, let's go with SQLite then. What about vector search for memory recall?
sqlite-vec is a good fit — it's a SQLite extension for vector similarity search, no separate vector DB needed, and it embeds into the same file as everything else.
Perfect, use sqlite-vec. One more thing — what embedding model should we default to?
mxbai-embed-large via Ollama — it's a 1024-dim embedding model that runs locally, matching our fully-offline requirement.
Sounds good, go ahead and wire that up as the default.
Done. I've set the default embed provider to Ollama with mxbai-embed-large and the vector store to sqlite-vec backed by better-sqlite3.

gold_atoms.text: Use SQLite (via better-sqlite3), not Postgres, for astramemory-local's storage — a local-first daemon should not require a separate server process.
Use sqlite-vec for vector similarity search instead of a separate vector database.
Default embedding model is mxbai-embed-large via Ollama (1024-dim), to keep embedding fully local/offline.
